questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) Scarcely had the newly appointed Director of Intelligence assumed her post / (2) when a sophisticated cyber-espionage campaign was detected / (3) within the high-security servers of the national defense agency, / (4) prompted an immediate and total lockdown of all external communication channels.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Scarcely had the newly appointed Director of Intelligence assumed her post / (2) when a sophisticated cyber-espionage campaign was detected / (3) within the high-security servers of the national defense agency, / (4) prompted an immediate and total lockdown of all external communication channels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. prompted an immediate and total lockdown of all external communication channels.

Key Points

  • The error lies in part (4), where the word "prompted" is used incorrectly. It disrupts the logical flow and grammatical accuracy of the sentence.
  • The word "prompted" should be replaced with "prompting", as the sentence requires a participial form to indicate an ongoing action resulting from the detection of the cyber-espionage campaign.
  • Correct usage: "prompting an immediate and total lockdown of all external communication channels".

Correct sentence: Scarcely had the newly appointed Director of Intelligence assumed her post when a sophisticated cyber-espionage campaign was detected within the high-security servers of the national defense agency, prompting an immediate and total lockdown of all external communication channels.

Additional Information

  • Scarcely...when: This construction is used for emphasizing that one event happens immediately after another.
  • Participial phrases: When describing actions that are consequences or results, participial phrases (e.g., "prompting") are commonly used.
  • Correct verb forms: Ensure the verb aligns with the subject and complements the intended meaning.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence/s: (a) The wages of sin are death. (b) I have many works to do. (c) Do not be friends with selfish people.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the incorrect sentence/s:

(a) The wages of sin are death.

(b) I have many works to do.

(c) Do not be friends with selfish people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ' (a) and (b)'.
Key Points
  • The error in sentence (a), "The wages of sin are death," is regarding its verb agreement. The phrase is a well-known expression from the Bible (Romans 6:23) and correctly uses "is" instead of "are." The corrected sentence should be "The wages of sin is death," treating "wages" in a singular conceptual sense.
  • Sentence (b), "I have many works to do," incorrectly uses "works" to refer to tasks or jobs. In English, "work" is an uncountable noun when referring to tasks or employment and does not typically use a plural form in this context. The correct sentence should be "I have much work to do."
  • Sentence (c), "Do not be friends with selfish people," has no grammatical errors and conveys a clear, correct statement as advised in various social and ethical teachings.
  • Therefore, the sentences (a) and (b) are incorrect because of verb agreement issues and misuse of a plural form for an uncountable noun, respectively.
Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 2'

Direction: In the following question, the 1st and the last part of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts and named P, Q, R and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find out which of the four combinations is correct.

1. India is known for its diversity all over the globe.

P. The traditional Indian attire has earned admirers from people from all over to organizations like UNESCO.

Q. Ethnic clothing is just one of the things that distinguish one part of India from the other.

R. The craftsmanship with which artisans create traditional dresses is really incredible.

S. All forms of clothing are quite labour-intensive and require a lot of attention to detail.

6. Many of these art forms are dying because the cost of production is higher and few people can afford to pay the high cost of the dress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘QPRS’.
Key Points
  • While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them.
  • Let us see how these parts of the sentence/paragraph can be arranged properly.
    • Sentence Q follows Sentence 1 as it establishes the subject matter by talking about the Ethnic clothing.
    • Hence, it'll be the first Sentence after 1. Therefore, Q follows 1.
    • Sentence P is the logical successor of Sentence Q because it's adding further information to the context as it is saying about Indian attire. Therefore, P follows Q.
    • Sentence R is the logical successor of Sentence P because as it is tlaking about the craftmanship which helps to create attire.
    • Sentence S is directly connected with Sentence 6. Therefore, R follows P. 
    • Sentence S is the logical successor of Sentence R because it's providing a conclusion to the context as it is talking about different forms of clothing and is directly connected to Sentence 6. Therefore, S follows R. 
  • Thus, the correct order is QPRS:
     

1. India is known for its diversity all over the globe.

Q. Ethnic clothing is just one of the things that distinguish one part of India from the other.

P. The traditional Indian attire has earned admirers from people from all over to organizations like UNESCO.

R. The craftsmanship with which artisans create traditional dresses is really incredible.

S. All forms of clothing are quite labour-intensive and require a lot of attention to detail.

6. Many of these art forms are dying because the cost of production is higher and few people can afford to pay the high cost of the dress.

Additional Information

  • Para-Jumble refers to a paragraph wherein the sentences forming it are jumbled.
  • We are required to arrange the sentences in a proper manner such that they link and form a coherent paragraph.
  • The name of the topic is in a way misleading because we are not jumbling paragraphs here but we are actually straightening out jumbled sentences in a paragraph.
  • This type of question is actually pretty common in various competitive exams and in recent years.

questions.solution:

Key Points 

  • The expression 'A lot of' as well as 'A number of' is succeeded by the plural noun and plural verb according to the subject-verb agreement.
    • Example: 
      • A lot of students are attending the seminar.

  • Therefore, from the above-given explanation, it is clear that statements (i) and (iv) are grammatically correct.

Additional Information

  •  Subject-verb agreement: It states that the verb corresponding to the singular subject will be singular and the verb corresponding to the plural subject will be plural.
    • Example:

Additional Information

  • Escorts: means to accompany someone or something somewhere.

questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In the following question, the 1st and the last part of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts and named P, Q, R and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find out which of the four combinations is correct.

1. Independence Day is one of the most important days of the year for our country. 

P. The British has taken over a lot of the world and India was one of its many colonies.

Q. For hundreds of years India was ruled by the United Kingdom and our country was a part of the British Empire.

R. It means we were free to rule ourselves and were not ruled by anyone else.

S. Each year on August 15 we celebrate the day we became an independent nation.

6. Before they came, India was made up of many kingdoms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘SRQP’.
Key Points
  • While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them.
  • Let us see how these parts of the sentence/paragraph can be arranged properly.
    • Sentence S follows Sentence 1 as it establishes the subject matter by providing an introductory information about Independence Day.
    • Hence, it'll be the first Sentence after 1. Therefore, S follows 1. 
    • Sentence R is the logical successor of Sentence S because it's providing further information about the meaning of 'Independence'. Therefore, R follows S.
    • Sentence Q is the logical successor of Sentence R because it is adding more information to the context by talking about the ruling of the British Empire in India. Therefore, Q follows R.
    • Sentence P is the logical successor of Sentence Q because it's providing a conclusion to the context by adding more information to the ruling of the British in India. Therefore, P follows Q. 
  • Thus, the correct order is SRQP:
     

1. Independence Day is one of the most important days of the year for our country. 

S. Each year on August 15 we celebrate the day we became an independent nation.

R. It means we were free to rule ourselves and were not ruled by anyone else.

Therefore, the correct answer is They hinder species' ability to migrate and adjust to warming temperatures.

questions.question: Based on the passage's discussion of the post-revolutionary settlement, it can be reasonably inferred that the author believes a true social revolution requires:
questions.questionHtml: Based on the passage's discussion of the post-revolutionary settlement, it can be reasonably inferred that the author believes a true social revolution requires:

options.text: The absolute preservation of existing property relations and colonial class structures without any state interference.
options.html: The absolute preservation of existing property relations and colonial class structures without any state interference.

options.text: A fundamental upending and restructuring of the socio-economic matrix, rather than a mere transfer of sovereign authority between elite classes.
options.html: A fundamental upending and restructuring of the socio-economic matrix, rather than a mere transfer of sovereign authority between elite classes.

options.text: The complete mobilization of the merchant aristocracy to permanently safeguard lucrative, illicit trade networks.

options.text: Merely substituting a domestic oligarchy for a foreign imperial elite while keeping localized legal codes identical.
options.html: Merely substituting a domestic oligarchy for a foreign imperial elite while keeping localized legal codes identical.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.
 
Key Points
  • Why Option 2 is correct:
    • The author argues that the American Revolution was fundamentally an "elite-driven transfer of sovereign authority rather than a social revolution." Because the movement insulated the existing class structure and merely substituted a foreign elite with a domestic oligarchy without radically upturning the socio-economic matrix, it can be reasonably inferred that a true social revolution would require a fundamental restructuring of that very socio-economic matrix.
  • Why Option 1 is incorrect:
    • The preservation of existing class structures and property relations is exactly why the author classifies the American Revolution as a conservative movement rather than a true social revolution.
  • Why Option 3 is incorrect:
    • Mobilizing the merchant aristocracy to protect their illicit networks was an element of the elite-driven secessionist movement, which the author contrasts with a deep social restructuring.
  • Why Option 4 is incorrect:
    • Substituting a domestic oligarchy for a foreign imperial elite is explicitly described as the limitation of the post-revolutionary settlement, rather than the definition of a true social revolution.
Therefore, the correct answer is A fundamental upending and restructuring of the socio-economic matrix, rather than a mere transfer of sovereign authority between elite classes.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: Incorrect because protecting the colonial class system directly prevented the emergence of an egalitarian social shift.
  • Option 3: Incorrect because the merchant class acted out of material self-interest to shield their regional wealth, not to trigger social transformation.
  • Option 4: Incorrect because this substitution describes a political transfer of power that left the underlying societal inequities completely intact.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the primary systemic catalyst for Great Britain attempting to rationalize imperial administration and enforce mercantilist regulations?

Key Points
  • Why Option 3 is correct:

It notes that "Faced with a staggering national debt incurred while defending its American possessions, the British Parliament sought to rationalize imperial administration and enforce long-neglected mercantilist regulations" following the Seven Years' War.
  • Why Option 1 is incorrect:

  • Why Option 4 is incorrect:
    • The colonial merchant assemblies fiercely resisted these administrative changes because they presented an existential threat to the highly lucrative and autonomous trade networks they had enjoyed under salutary neglect.
Therefore, the correct answer is A staggering national debt accumulated by the British state during the course of the Seven Years' War.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: Incorrect because Whig philosophy served as a rhetorical tool for colonial rebellion rather than a British policy catalyst.
  • Option 2: Incorrect because the Southern plantocracy was wealthy and motivated by preserving its lucrative economic position.
  • Option 4: Incorrect because the change in British policy was a top-down mandate opposed by colonial leadership rather than a local request.
